scenarios.designer_intent:
The map is meant as an entry point to help readers understand the visualizations below it. Both the map and the following charts use 100 dots (100%) that are distributed differently.
It also serves as a transition between the hourglass on the left (about how the world population has developed) and the charts under the map that connect population distribution to other global comparisons, such as CO2 consumption and wealth vs. poverty.
The map gives an immediate sense of how unevenly the world population is distributed and sets up comparisons like: relatively few people live in North America, but CO2 consumption is disproportionately high.
scenarios.query: Retrieve visualization guidelines relevant to this chart and intent, aiming to improve the visualization for a general news reader audience.
scenarios.title: Population distribution by continent

scenarios.designer_intent:
If I remember correctly, the plan was to first show a comparison across EU countries (and where Austria stands on the gender pay gap) and then move into Austria-specific data. This chart is essentially the Austria-specific counterpart to the EU bar chart.
It suggests an urban-rural gap and possibly a west-east gradient. The most important message is the “level of old-age pensions in comparison”: whether someone worked full time or part time has a substantial negative impact on women later on. The topic of childcare is also included.
scenarios.query: Retrieve visualization guidelines relevant to this chart and intent, aiming to improve the visualization for a general news reader audience.
scenarios.title: Austria gender pay gap by region

scenarios.designer_intent:

Vienna has relatively few beds overall, but the most beds per business.

scenarios.designer_intent:
This chart was published alongside the release of new Q4/2022 data. Given COVID-19's impact on the labour market, the intent was to show whether the situation is “recovering” (i.e., change over time). Because a static chart cannot show many time points for 27 EU countries plus the EU aggregate and three EFTA countries, the chart compares Q4/2022 with one year earlier (Q4/2021).
This lets readers see the change for every country, focusing on what users typically care about most: their own country, and comparisons to other countries of interest.
scenarios.query: Retrieve visualization guidelines relevant to this chart and intent, aiming to improve the visualization for a general news reader audience.
scenarios.title: Recent job starters (Q4 2021 vs Q4 2022)

scenarios.designer_intent:
This chart was published alongside new population projection data. It uses a standard population pyramid split by men and women to show the age distribution today (2022) and projected for 2100.
For orientation, ages are grouped into three broader bands (children, working age, elderly). Readers can visually see the pyramid “shift upward”: the share of older people increases substantially, changing the overall shape.
scenarios.query: Retrieve visualization guidelines relevant to this chart and intent, aiming to improve the visualization for a general news reader audience.
scenarios.title: EU population pyramid (2022 and 2100)
